batch_002_findings.dangling_references_found: 4 (T-0006, T-0008, T-0010, T-0011) plus 1 numbering gap (T-0009), all originating in batch 001, all detected by §37 check 4. Second consecutive batch in which this check caught a real defect.
batch_002_findings.corpus_not_self_contained: G-0007 - load-bearing instruments cited throughout the window live outside docs/knowledgeos/ and are therefore outside the 3081-entry registry entirely. Escalated to §49: this is a SCOPE finding, not a batch finding.
batch_002_findings.check_14_defect: CHECK 14 AS SPECIFIED IS WRONG, found by running it. It flags F0016 because a cited-artifact date_event shares the VALUE 2026-08-03 with historical_sequence_date. But F0016 derives that date from its own COMMISSION event (applies_to: THIS_FILE); the external research input merely happens to be same-day. The check tests VALUE COINCIDENCE where it should test PROVENANCE. Correct predicate: reject only if NO applies_to=THIS_FILE event supports historical_sequence_date. Under the corrected predicate F0016 passes and all 15 batch-002 rows pass. Classified as a PROTOCOL DEFECT (AUDIT-05), not a data defect. Same-day citation is common in this corpus, so the false-positive rate of the specified check would be high at scale.
batch_002_findings.canonical_discovery_failure: SELF-OBSERVED, recorded not repaired. The Step-2 protocol was drafted WITHOUT searching docs/knowledgeos/backlog/, the folder it was being written into. EKS-35 already registered findings F-1/F-2 (timestamps do not encode argument order) from 2026-09-09, with stronger evidence. This is a further occurrence of proposing-before-searching - the failure mode T-0023 counts and F0015 records as occurrence #11. It also drew on an INDEXED region, corroborating C-0006: the cause is not only a missing index but an unread one. Consequences: gate G2-F and quality gate Q10 added to the Step-2 proposal; obligations RO-0015/RO-0016 opened.
